A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BracketIRE/TMRNet work, despite v5's changed title. Text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and can be matched across the reorganization.

before.justification: v4 reports original experiments on synthesized image pairs and captured nighttime smartphone images, including benchmark comparisons and architectural and adaptation ablations.

after.justification: v5 retains these original results and adds HDR and BurstSR evaluations, an AdaIR comparison, and a staged-processing experiment in Appendices C–E.

M1.justification: The common and frame-specific aggregation modules, synthetic pretraining, and self-supervised adaptation with temporal and EMA losses remain unchanged. Four-channel RAW packing is newly clarified documentation; the added comparison pipelines do not revise the proposed method.

E1.justification: v5 retains the constructed synthetic and smartphone datasets and adds evaluations on the Kalantari HDR dataset and BurstSR, including synthetic-to-real burst adaptation. Appendix C substantially broadens validation to additional data distributions and standalone HDR reconstruction and burst super-resolution tasks.

E2.justification: The original ten external baselines remain. v5 adds optical-flow-aligned AdaIR and a separately trained denoising–deblurring–HDR cascade in Appendices D–E. Table 2 also includes unadapted TMRNet as a comparator, using scores already reported in v4's appendix.

E3.justification: Original splits, training budgets, metrics, and boundary exclusions are retained. New controls introduce aligned and concatenated AdaIR inputs and separately trained, cascaded processing stages. Appendix Eq. (B) changes the conditional Gaussian's second parameter from 0.3 to 0.3^2; this revises the reported simulation setting without establishing that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix E adds a targeted ablation comparing joint processing against sequential denoising, deblurring, and HDR reconstruction. Appendix C.2 extends the with/without-adaptation analysis to BurstSR. Existing frame-count, exposure-combination, module-depth, and loss-weight ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for the evaluated methods. v5 continues reporting point estimates; the revised synthetic-noise distribution is not experimental uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark and ablation scores are retained. New results include TMRNet at 42.43 dB on Kalantari HDR and 48.92 dB on BurstSR, plus a separate BurstSR adaptation improvement from 44.70 to 45.57 dB. AdaIR scores 38.06 dB and staged processing 37.93 dB against joint TMRNet's 39.35 dB. These are additional comparisons, not improvements to the original reported scores.

T1.justification: Appendix Eq. (B) changes the conditional Gaussian specification for log read-noise parameters from a second argument of 0.3 to 0.3^2. This is a limited mathematical correction. The image-formation, aggregation, and adaptation equations otherwise retain their substance; renaming the mapping operator from S to M is not a theoretical change.

C1.justification: The title and abstract replace task-unification wording with obtaining a high-quality image by combining tasks. Both versions still claim the same four-task framework, TMRNet, self-supervised adaptation, datasets, and favorable comparative performance. The scientific scope of the main contributions is retained.

C2.justification: v5 adds explanations of interpolation-related simulation gaps, inference-time versus FLOPs tradeoffs, and staged processing's residual-blur-induced training/testing mismatch. Appendix G strengthens the interpretation of frame-count results into an argument that additional frames cannot worsen performance, without new supporting analysis. The sensor-generalization limitation is relocated unchanged.

D1.justification: v5 clarifies four-channel RAW packing, Alexa camera parameters for RGB-to-RAW conversion, and the rationale for existing border exclusions. It documents the new comparison pipelines and points to higher-resolution supplementary images. Conversely, v4's explicit code/data license statement and pretrained-model availability statement are omitted; actual resource withdrawal is not established.

R1.justification: Appendix D newly distinguishes this work from all-in-one restoration, citing AdaIR and Perceive-IR. v5 also adds Digital Gimbal and newer interpolation references and removes Delbracio and Sapiro's burst-deblurring reference. The broader positioning relative to burst, dual-exposure, and HDR processing remains intact.

P1.justification: v5 retitles the paper, revises unification terminology, changes citation style, and adds acknowledgments and corresponding-author identification. Applications and limitations move into Section 8, references precede the appendix, and implementation details gain subsections. The core narrative and method exposition remain largely unchanged.

P2.justification: The ICLR formatting substantially redistributes figures and tables throughout the document. Table 1 is reformatted, Table 2 separates adapted and unadapted TMRNet rows, and four new result tables appear as Tables B–E. Existing qualitative examples are retained, with Figure B embedded at higher resolution and several captions expanded.

improvement.justification: The external benchmarks and joint-versus-staged control strengthen the empirical support beyond v4's constructed datasets. Clearer implementation explanations and explicit adaptation rows improve transparency. However, the new benchmark protocols remain sparsely documented, and explicit license and pretrained-model disclosures are reduced, making the net quality gain useful but limited.
